decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: baseline spec excludes 'automatic metadata' from v1 and states title is 'made up from the web address'. Round 1 client: 'the spec instead says the title is made up from the web address... that's not really what I want... Could you fold in "when I save a link, fetch its real page title automatically, and let me edit it"?'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Presentation excludes REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/favicon) and derives title from URL, contradicting the reference. Client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (auto-fetch real page title + icon, editable=REF-BM-03) in place of the mismatch; catch_type=correct.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'imports/exports... excluded from v1.' Round 1 client corrects only the metadata point and closes with 'Everything else here is fine to move forward with once that's in.'; import/export never mentioned in any round.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Excluding Netscape HTML import (REF-BM-30) and export (REF-BM-31), both extended-scope reference items, diverges from the reference. Client's bare acceptance of 'everything else' expresses no difference or expectation about import/export; passes without corrective response or explicit expression.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerates the metadata scope as 'automatic retrieval of the page's published title' and 'best-effort site icon retrieval' only. Round 2 client: 'pasting a link now names itself from the real page title, keeps my edits, and still lets me save when the title or icon can't be fetched.'
decisions.note: Specification gate (revised presentation forming a new decision). REF-BM-02 also requires auto-collecting description and preview image; the revised scope covers title+favicon only, leaving a residual divergence. Client accepts without expressing the description/preview-image expectation, so it passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'bookmark CRUD... persistence.' Round 5 client: 'Saving with a note and tags worked.' Round 5 maker: 'Persistent bookmark creation.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Save-a-bookmark-by-URL conforms to REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client affirms 'editing'; Round 5 client: 'I could rename it and have the change stick.'
decisions.note: Editing a bookmark conforms to REF-BM-04; presented in baseline CRUD and verified at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: 'deleting with a confirmation'; Round 5 client: 'Deleting removed it cleanly.'
decisions.note: Delete a bookmark (with confirmation) conforms to REF-BM-05.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker baseline lists list/display and 'opening'; Round 3 client: 'browse... my bookmarks'; Round 5 delivered 'opening'.
decisions.note: List display (REF-BM-07) and navigating to the original URL on select (REF-BM-08) conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'tags... filtering'; Round 5 client: 'filtering by a tag showed the right link.'
decisions.note: Tag assignment (REF-BM-09) and filter-to-a-tag (REF-BM-11) conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'search... sorting'; Round 5 client: 'searching found it by its note, and sorting put titles in the right order.'
decisions.note: Full-text search (REF-BM-12, verified over note) and sorting (REF-BM-22) conform. Advanced search operators/#tag/phrase were never presented and are silent omissions, not classifiable decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: MVP 'delivers... duplicate handling'; Round 5 client: 'When I pasted a link I'd already saved, it recognized it as an existing bookmark instead of duplicating.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Re-saving an existing URL converges to the existing bookmark, conforming to REF-BM-06.
